subject: Coupa invite / login flow: legacy IdP loses session during OTP step
messages:
From: Maya Thompson <onboarding@vendorpulse.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: support@vendorpulse.com
Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2029 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Coupa invite failing to accept — redirect loses OTP

Hi Vivek,

We ran into an issue accepting the Coupa supplier invite this morning. When our admin clicks the invite link we get redirected to our IdP for authentication (SAML), then back to Redwood but the OTP challenge never shows — the session appears to be dropped mid-redirect. We tried in Chrome and Firefox; same result.

I've attached a screenshot of the network flow and a small debug log from our end (sso_debug.log.txt). The behaviour started after we migrated one of our legacy IdP proxies to a new load balancer that terminates SSL. Our engineering team suspects session affinity is not preserved across the proxy handoff.

Can someone from your side confirm whether Redwood expects a sticky session or a particular header (X-Forwarded-For / X-Forwarded-Proto) to be preserved during the SAML relay? This is blocking our ability to finish vendor setup — PO routing is held up until we accept and provide W9.

Thanks,
Maya Thompson
Vendor Onboarding Lead
VendorPulse

Hi Maya — thanks for the detailed repro and attachments.

I'm looping in Ben (platform infra) and Priyom (partner ops) to take a look. Quick answers up front: we do not strictly require "sticky" sessions at the application level — the SAML flow should be stateless if RelayState and the SAMLResponse are round-tripped correctly. That said, some proxy/load-balancer configurations that rewrite cookies or strip certain headers can break intermediate state (especially when we rely on an ephemeral binding cookie during the redirect).

Ben/Priyom — can you validate whether our Coupa invite endpoints are sensitive to session cookie rewriting or non-standard relaystate handling? Maya, we'll follow up with an ask list.

Proposed next step: a short 30-minute debugging call today if that works for you (I added a Zoom link below). If possible please send the full SAML request/response (if you can share) and the exact set of request headers around the redirect.

Subject: Re: Coupa invite failing to accept — redirect loses OTP

Thanks Vivek / Maya — digging in.

Quick technical notes from the infra side:
- Our invite flow uses a short-lived signing cookie (inv_state) that binds the SAML relay to the in-progress invite. If that cookie is dropped or rewritten, the backend treats the session as new and won't surface the OTP step (it falls back).
- The common culprits: aggressive proxy cookie rewriting, SameSite changes, or TLS termination that strips/normalizes the Host/Origin headers.

Maya — from your sso_debug.log I see the relaystate present but the final POST to /auth/saml/acs is missing the inv_state cookie. Can you confirm whether your new load balancer is doing cookie re-write rules? Also, does it insert or strip the "X-Forwarded-Host" header? Even if your IdP is returning SAMLResponse successfully, if the binding cookie wasn't forwarded back to us we will not display the OTP challenge.

If you can't share the full SAMLResponse publicly, please at minimum capture request headers for the POST to /auth/saml/acs and DM them to me. For a short-term workaround we can allow a relaystate-only path (we'll point to a fallback token) but that requires a quick config change on our side and a brief maintenance window (5–10 mins) — I'll coordinate with our infra ops once we get confirmation from Maya.

Attachment: ben-debug-steps.txt (contains curl examples to capture headers).

-ben
Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Hi Ben — thanks for the quick analysis. Agree that the inv_state cookie is the missing piece. Our infra team confirmed the new F5 load balancer was configured to strip non-standard cookies during a rewrite rule applied for cross-domain session normalization. That's likely the change that introduced this.

I've attached an excerpt from our proxy logs showing the cookie header before and after the handoff. We'll run a temporary rule to preserve cookies named inv_state and saml_binding for the invite path and then re-test.

We can be on the Zoom you proposed at 14:00 PT if that helps to validate live.

—Maya
